items.action: Disable IBE support (config system encryption ibe -> set status disable) and block the management interface from the internet until the patched build for your branch is available.
items.details: Affects FortiMail 8.0.0-8.0.1, 7.6.0-7.6.6, 7.4.0-7.4.8 and 7.2.0-7.2.9. Fixes land in 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2; 7.2 users must upgrade to the 7.4 branch or later. Fortinet published IOCs including attacker IPs 79.141.169.187 and 45.129.0.192 and backdoor-style files such as /data/lib/liblog.so. CISA added the flaw to the KEV catalog with a federal mitigation deadline of October 4.
items.summary: Fortinet is warning that CVE-2026-104286 (FG-IR-26-175), a CVSS 9.8 path-traversal flaw in the FortiMail management interface, is being actively exploited to write arbitrary files and execute code on vulnerable devices.
items.title: FortiMail zero-day under active attack — check your appliance now

items.action: Upgrade Mooncake past 0.3.13.post1 and restrict the HTTP metadata server to trusted networks.
items.details: Attackers can poison segment descriptors or re-create rpc_meta entries to redirect KV-cache transfers to attacker-controlled listeners, or exhaust server memory. Disclosed October 2; no KEV listing or public exploit code confirmed yet.
items.summary: Mooncake through 0.3.13.post1 has a missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-103765, CVSS 9.4) in its HTTP metadata server /metadata handler, letting unauthenticated attackers read, overwrite and delete transfer-engine metadata.
items.title: Mooncake KV-cache metadata hijack: unauthenticated access (CVSS 9.4)

items.action: Update n8n to 1.123.80+ (1.x) or 2.40.1+ (2.x) and review shared-workflow editor permissions.
items.details: Also fixed: CVE-2026-103246 (CVSS 7.7) — missing credential-ownership validation during inline agent node-tool introspection lets attackers reference arbitrary credential IDs to decrypt and exfiltrate plaintext secrets to attacker-controlled hosts. Both flaws published October 1; no known exploitation.
items.summary: n8n before 1.123.80 has a credential-tampering flaw (CVE-2026-103247, CVSS 8.5) where duplicate node IDs bypass the workflow credential tamper guard, letting an attacker with editor access to shared workflows steal victim credentials and redirect secrets to attacker-controlled hosts.
items.title: n8n credential tampering via duplicate node IDs (CVE-2026-103247)

items.details: Published October 1 as GHSA-q55r-w7fh-rmh6; no known exploitation.
items.summary: Ghost 6.20.0 through 6.57.1 has a session-handling flaw (CVE-2026-103283, CVSS 8.1) that lets an authenticated staff user log in as any other staff user with just the password, bypassing two-factor authentication.
items.title: Ghost CMS staff auth bypass defeats 2FA (CVE-2026-103283)

items.action: Update jackson-dataformats-binary to the patched release per GHSA-3v8f-v6vx-fmrm.
items.details: Both rated High (CVSS 7.5), disclosed October 1. No public exploit code confirmed; not in CISA KEV.
items.summary: FasterXML jackson-dataformats-binary never enforces the maxNameLength limit on CBOR/Smile property names — a single unbounded property name exhausts parser memory, an unauthenticated DoS on any endpoint parsing untrusted binary documents (CVE-2026-68495 for CBOR, CVE-2026-68496 for Smile).
items.title: Jackson CBOR/Smile parser memory-exhaustion DoS (CVE-2026-68495/68496)

items.details: The Gentlemen also claimed Hollard Insurance earlier in September; stolen data in that case traced back to a third party too (MIP Holdings' June 2026 incident).
items.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group listed Guardrisk, an insurer under South Africa's Momentum Group, on its dark-web leak site — but Guardrisk says its own systems are uncompromised and customer data exposure came from a cyber incident at third-party CoverCubed.
items.title: The Gentlemen claims Guardrisk breach via third-party CoverCubed

items.details: Listed as a threat-actor claim — the victim has not publicly confirmed a breach.
items.summary: Akira added building-materials supplier DPL Group to its leak site on October 1, threatening to publish 8 GB of corporate data including employee personal documents, financials and customer information.
items.title: Akira claims DPL Group, threatens 8 GB data leak

items.details: All remain unconfirmed threat-actor claims at this stage; monitoring via ThreatMon dark-web tracking, observed October 1.
items.summary: New October 1 leak-site listings: Chaos claims dental provider Park Dental, inCransom lists a metal recycling firm, and the Genesis operation lists Owens Distributors.
items.title: Leak-site churn: Chaos, inCransom and Genesis post new victims

items.details: Public reporting places the BrainCipher attack around September 23 and the lawsuit filing on September 26.
items.summary: A borrower sued Gold Star Mortgage Financial Group on September 26, just three days after the BrainCipher ransomware group claimed the Ann Arbor lender's customer data was stolen — one of the fastest claim-to-lawsuit turnarounds of 2026.
items.title: Gold Star Mortgage sued days after BrainCipher ransomware claim

items.details: Per the October 1 weekly intelligence report; target technology was web applications, objective data leak and financial gain.
items.summary: Krybit ransomware attacked an Indian construction company and published its data, per the October 1 weekly intelligence report.
items.title: Krybit ransomware hits a construction company in India

items.details: Other items in the October 1 roundup: a Kanpur probe exposing a 611-account dispersal network after a Rs 48.20-lakh digital-arrest fraud, and Punjab Police battling 50+ AI-generated videos after the LPU unrest.
items.summary: The cabinet cleared a Rs 1,789.52-crore AI-powered traffic system for Delhi Police; Chandauli and Delhi police busted international cyberfraud call centres targeting elderly Japanese and American victims; and Telangana launched its 'Pause. Think. Verify' campaign for Cybersecurity Awareness Month.
items.title: Delhi Police clears Rs 1,789.52-cr AI traffic system; call centres busted
